page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.e4.large is an x86_64 architecture server instance powered by a shared Intel Xeon E5-2682 v4 processor running at 2.5 GHz. It features 2 vCPUs, which correspond to 2 physical cores with 1.0 thread per core. The instance is equipped with 16.0 GB of system memory, yielding a high memory-to-core ratio of 8.0 GB per core. It does not include local storage or dedicated GPU hardware, and the baseline network bandwidth is rated at 0 Gbps. The hypervisor managing this instance is KVM.

Benchmark data indicates that the ecs.e4.large sits in the lower performance tiers. In CPU-focused tests, the instance achieved a stress-ng single-core score of 945.88 and a multi-core score of 1857.99, both falling into the bottom 10% of benchmarked servers. Memory performance is similarly constrained, with a read-only large block bandwidth of 14.95 GB/sec and a write large block bandwidth of 11.46 GB/sec, both categorized in the bottom 10%. Database operations via Passmark scored 558.24, and Redis SET operations reached 2.53 million operations per second, placing the instance in the bottom 25% for these workloads.

Given the shared CPU allocation and the older Intel Xeon architecture, this instance is positioned as a budget-oriented option where memory capacity is prioritized over raw compute speed. The 1:8 vCPU-to-RAM ratio provides a high resource density for memory-bound tasks that do not require sustained high-performance CPU throughput. Tradeoffs include poor performance in CPU-intensive calculations, such as LLM inference where prompt processing for a small 135M model is limited to 86.12 tokens per second. This server is best suited for lightweight memory-intensive workloads, basic web serving, or development environments that can tolerate shared CPU resource limits.
